title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
why: B-type evaluation lead: a closed-loop benchmark where frozen frontier VLMs control a camera in ManiSkill3/SAPIEN indoor scenes through a shared 10-tool interface (pose/intrinsics queries, move/rotate/capture, triangulation, submit_positions, finish_mapping) to build an object-center map under bounded interaction budgets. Directly tests harnessed VLM agents on active embodied spatial construction rather than open-loop VQA.
mechanism: Shared tool-calling harness over frozen VLMs: list_entities, get_camera_pose/intrinsics, set_camera_position, move_camera, rotate_camera, capture_image, triangulate_observations, submit_positions, finish_mapping. No tool reveals ground-truth centers or scores. Agent explores from an initial RGB view, acquires further calibrated views, and revises an explicit object-center map; validator checks identifiers, finite coords, and a public radius bound. Scenes assembled in SAPIEN via ManiSkill3 (iTHOR/RoboTHOR/ArchitecTHOR/ReplicaCAD/ProcTHOR).
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: 80 scenes, one episode per model–scene; 7 frontier VLMs (GPT-6 Astra/Sol, Claude Opus/Sonnet 5.5, Kimi-K3, Qwen3.8-Max, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) under identical prompts/tools; object-scale overlap / IoU-style coverage metrics jointly scoring localization and target coverage; qualitative analysis and protocol appendices. Embodiment is camera-only active mapping (no arm/nav base)—scope borderline but closed-loop tool harness in physical indoor sim.
